text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need final calls for GA readiness by EOD Friday. Focus: SLA levels (hosted/dedicated/private), pricing meter & burst billing, docs MVP, and oncall routing for SLA tiers. Who's got bandwidth to lock decisions?

Sanjay: I can take SLA wording. Proposal: Hosted API = 99.9% monthly, Dedicated = 99.95% with reserved pools, Private = contractual SLA (customer-managed infra caveat). Thoughts? :eyes:

Zoe: Pricing note — if we lock 99.9 for hosted, we need to model costs for the tail (extra capacity) and burst pricing. Proposal: baseline per-token + burst multiplier applied after sustained 5m > capacity. Keeps cost predictable.

Ellie: Docs scope: must include one-pager SLA summary, dedicated provisioning checklist, and a short runbook for oncall. Keep it minimal for GA — links to full runbooks later. I can ship the one-pager and checklist.

Rafael: Oncall routing: SLA tiers need different routing. Hosted SLA incidents -> Platform SRE rotation (24/7). Dedicated SLA -> Dedicated infra oncall first, platform as fallback. Private -> Customer support + SE on the hook; platform only if it's our control plane. We need clear ownership in the SLA doc.

Maya: Agreed. Sanjay, can you draft the SLA table (levels, targets, credits) and put a line about scope exclusions (networking, customer infra for Private)?

Sanjay: Yep. Rough table I'm thinking:
- Hosted: 99.9% uptime, monthly uptime window, service credits tiered (0.5%, 1.5%).
- Dedicated: 99.95% uptime, guaranteed concurrency, credits + pool capacity backstop.
- Private: No baseline SLA unless we operate infra; otherwise "best effort" + enterprise negotiation.

Zoe: For pricing, we need to call out burst multiplier and minimum invoice. Example: baseline 0.0006 $/token, burst multiplier 2.5x after 5m sustained > reserved. Also call out dedicated reservations (monthly commit) with discount tiers.

Ellie: I'll add a short example billing table to the docs so customers understand invoicing. Also: we should include a "how to test your workload" section to reduce false positives on SLO alerts.

Rafael: Speaking of alerts — propose these three core monitors for GA: p95 token latency, p99 tail latency, and 5m error rate. Immediate pages on sustained p99 > 1s or error rate > 1% for 10m. Draft alert rule:```
alert: HighTailLatency
expr: p99(request_token_latency_seconds) > 1.0
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
```

Maya: Nice. Add an annotation to the alert about affected models (model_id label) and whether the request hit the cache or not. That will speed triage.

Sanjay: Ops/degradation policy: if model nodes drop below 60% capacity, automatic fallback to a compatible lower-capacity variant (quantized) if enabled, otherwise degrade non-critical routes. Need this in the runtime FAQ.

Zoe: One more pricing edge: free trial credits + burst protection. We should limit free trial burst to a soft cap to avoid huge unexpected bills. Document that as "trial burst cap" with opt-in expansion via AE.

Ellie: Actions for docs: I'll draft SLA one-pager, a short "what to expect on support" section, and quick alert/playbook snippets. ETA: Wed EOD.

Sanjay: I'll put the SLA table + fallback policy in a PR by Tue noon.

Rafael: I'll export Prometheus alert rules and add runbook TODOs. Also will add runbook step: "tag incidents with model_id and deployment_type".

Zoe: I'll run pricing sim with the new burst multiplier assumptions and send a small spreadsheet. ETA Thu morning.

Maya: Great. Couple of quick decisions now so we can call GA next week:
1) Default SLA levels above (Hosted 99.9 / Dedicated 99.95) — any objections?
2) Burst multiplier = 2.5x default — ok?
3) Oncall routing as Rafael suggested — ok?

Sanjay: +1 to defaults.

Ellie: +1.

Rafael: +1, but flag: Dedicated customers may want custom routing. We'll note that in docs as an option.

Zoe: +1 to numbers, will validate with cost model.

DeployBot: deploy status update — staging: ga-readiness/sla-docs v0.8 deployed to staging at 1737777455. :rocket:

Maya: Awesome — we'll treat these as agreed defaults unless someone raises a critical blocker by Thu EOD. I'll create a short owners list and publish the GA checklist once we have the PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
